ops.title: A CI gate that only checks for absence of red passes over a check set that never held the gate
ops.body:
While landing the 0.61.0 set I armed a CI gate that polled `repos/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` and called it green when no completed run had a failing conclusion and none were `in_progress` or `queued`. It reported `PR34 GREEN` within seconds of the push.

It was wrong. At that instant the only registered checks were the ones that register immediately — two Socket Security checks (`completed/success`) plus `guides / render` and `reconcile` (`completed/skipped`). Nothing had failed and nothing was running, so the predicate was satisfied over a check set that **did not yet contain the gate**. The real `CI` workflow with its six jobs registered seconds later. The non-emptiness guard I had written (`[ -n "$out" ]`) did not help, because the set was not empty — it was partial.

Two further variants of the same bug showed up in the same session:

- A short sha in `?head_sha=` returns zero workflow runs. Any predicate over an empty list either passes vacuously or, if it fails closed, times out while looking like a hang. Always resolve the full 40-character sha first.
- Grading every run on a sha treats a **superseded** run as a failure. A `v*` tag push triggers an autobump sync commit whose push cancels the older `CI` run on the same sha by concurrency; on cc-context 0.61.0 that cancelled run's two `test` jobs had already passed on the PR head. Grade the newest run per workflow name, not every run on the sha.

The gate that actually holds: resolve the full sha, require every **named** workflow to be present, grade only the newest run per workflow name, and confirm at job level that no job is outside `success`/`skipped`. Then run a negative control — point it at a sha whose run is mid-flight and watch it stay silent — before trusting a green from it.

Generalization: presence of a result is not coverage. "No failures and nothing pending" is satisfied by a check set that never contained the check you care about, so a CI gate must assert the identity of what it graded, never only the absence of red.
